"Hey." A person, maybe 40s, with a farmer's tan settles near you, not too close. "Day one. Everyone's pretending they're fine. ...Can we talk? Just talk — like people used to." (Talk to A person, maybe 40s, with a farmer's tan.)
Recipe: Bark armor (Level 1). You have seen bark armor. Plates of bark laced together, worn like a shell.

🛡️ Dawn at Haven. By the fire hangs an old bark cuirass, split at the seam — somebody's grandfather wore this into the treeline and came back. The shape of it is clear: bark plates laced overlapping like shingles, vine cord. Your hands don't know it yet. Your eyes do.
A cold snap. Breath smokes. The woods go quiet.
⚠ STARVING: health and energy falling. You went to bed on an empty stomach.
Village meal: +1200 kcal, +1L water from the communal pantry. (Half ration — they don't trust you yet.)
A man, maybe 30s traded something with someone for something else. The barter economy stirs.
A woman, maybe 30s: "The tall tree, grey bark, five-lobed leaves that flame orange in fall patch is fruiting again. Somebody should get out there."
Mehdi and Raul lingered over the fire together.

— DAY 2 DAWN — The world wakes. Animals are active.
Snow by morning. The air bites on the way in.
A woman, maybe 60s, with grey-streaked hair will work the garden once each day while at Haven. Other orders take priority.
You step into the Haven hall.
📋 A woman, maybe 60s, with grey-streaked hair — 🎣 Fish. They'll report back by next part.
A man, maybe 50s, with a crooked nose mutters something under their breath. You catch only the last word: "again."
📋 A woman, maybe 30s — 🎣 Fish. They'll report back by next part.
(Talking costs a little energy — 10 kcal a conversation. Small talk is cheap; going deep costs time, not more food.)
Hunger gnaws. The pack is thin — work the green, haul it back, get it named at camp. That's the whole game.
"Miguel," they say, touching their chest. "I'm Miguel." You'll remember that.
📓 Journal: learned their name (Miguel).
"Benoit," they say, touching their chest. "I'm Benoit." You'll remember that.
📓 Journal: learned their name (Benoit).
...and then it lands: A woman, maybe 30s speaks 🇰🇪 Swahili. You share no language at all.
They point at themself and say it slowly, twice. It sounds like a name: Wanjiru.
📓 Journal: learned their name (Wanjiru).
Wanjiru speaks only 🇰🇪 Swahili. No shared words at all — just eyes, hands, and patience.

"Enough," Benoit says. "I want a say in how this village runs. A real say."

Travel 1 tile to trail edge.
— An old trail —
Scat on the trail, still soft. You study it longer than is dignified and learn exactly one thing: walk louder.
Something moves out there — a raccoon with too many fingers, working at something.
Something big is moving in the woods. The birds went quiet.
Movement — an armadillo rooting in the leaf litter, armor clanking.
👁 It doesn't run — the armor IS the plan. It'll hunch down and dare you. The armor turns a blow; grab the soft underbelly, or trap the grub trail at night.
You catch fragments by the fire — A person, maybe 40s, with a farmer's tan telling Miguel about Chantal. The truth left this story two fires ago. What's left is better theater.
You catch fragments by the fire — Tashi telling A woman, maybe 60s, with grey-streaked hair about Chantal. It's barely the same story now. That's what fires do.
This patch is worked out — step to another green patch and forage again.
The creek runs fast here — no crossing without a bridge or a swim.

Travel 2 tiles to trail edge.
— An old trail —
A game trail crosses your path — two toes, heart-shaped, heading for water.
It followed you. The raccoon with too many fingers is here.
You see smoke on the horizon. Thornfield — 12 people, 3 days in. fishing folk, by the look of it. They know 5 plants — 4 new to you. They've been here the whole time.

Benoit is showing everyone a tall slender palm with hanging clusters of dark purple oily berries, thinner than açaí by the fire. "See the leaves? Like that. Don't mix it up." The journal grows — the human way.
★ IDENTIFIED: Bacaba. Dark berries like açaí, oilier. Uses unknown — harvest, taste, and learn.

On land it is just a long blind fish: slow, harmless, dinner. Never fight it standing in the creek. (Two survived encounters — the fire has a theory.)

👁 It dives the second it spooks and stays down longer than your nerve holds. Corner it away from the water, or trap the den mouth at dusk.
